changes: Rāmagovindatīrtha: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the author's teacher, not a teacher connected with this copy.
Nārāyaṇatīrtha: roles reduced to 'author'. The Sāṅkhyacandrikā is his own work (itself a commentary on the Sāṅkhyakārikā), so 'commentator' was redundant.
Date: chronogram resolved. manu = 14, aṅka = 9, indu = 1, read right to left = 1914. Era left as unspecified (probably VS); ce_approx set to 1857.
Tithi and weekday normalized; Śrāvaṇa śukla 5 is Nāgapañcamī.

notes: The chronogram 'manvakendu' is taken as manv-aṅka-indu: manu = 14, aṅka = 9, indu = 1. Read right to left, this gives 1914. If 'aka' were instead read as arka (12), the number would not make sense. The era is not named. VS 1914 = c. 1857 CE fits; ŚS 1914 is impossible. I have not checked by calculation that Śrāvaṇa śukla 5 fell on a Sunday. Rāmagovindatīrtha appears only as the author's teacher. 'dvijarājacandrikā' is a pun on the title (dvijarāja = moon = candra). 'sudhīvara' ('best of the wise') is an honorific epithet of the scribe, not a caste name. 'lekhivān' is the cataloguer's (!), standing for alekhīt/likhitavān.
